title: Non-clashing teaching dimension versus VC dimension
formal: For every finite set X and every nonempty concept class \(C\subseteq 2^{x}\), is \(NCTD(C)\le \operatorname{VC}(C)\)? Equivalently, if C has VC dimension d, does there exist a teaching map assigning at most d correctly labeled examples to each concept such that no two distinct concepts are mutually consistent with one another’s assigned examples? Both positive and negative examples are allowed. The target constant is exactly one, not merely a bound \(O(d)\).
context:
The source and journal article give a universal upper bound quadratic in VC dimension. Their conclusion asks for the sharper inequality with coefficient one, and reports no counterexample to that inequality.

If a class of VC dimension d on X attains Sauer’s size bound \(\sum_{i=0}^{d} binomial(|X|,i)\), the cited representation-map result supplies a non-clashing map of size d. Maximum classes are a special case, not all finite classes.

The COLT 2024 paper constructs small maps for balls in particular graph classes and explicitly repeats the general open question. A size-four upper bound together with a VC-dimension-three upper bound for another family does not prove NCTD exceeds VC there.

The journal article separately studies stronger restrictions on avoiding collusion. Their optimal teaching parameter need not equal NCTD. Likewise, a map for the concepts themselves is not automatically a sample-compression scheme that must reconstruct from arbitrary samples.
why: Would show that every finite concept class can be taught with at most its VC dimension many examples per concept in the non-clashing model, giving a sharp link between learning capacity and teaching complexity.
status_note: Read the finite-domain no-clash definition and conclusion, the expanded JMLR treatment, and the COLT 2024 special-case results. Later searches through 12 September 2026 also found work on computing positive graph-ball teaching maps, but no proof or counterexample to the universal signed NCTD\(\le\)VC inequality. Search is not exhaustive.

upgraded_from.title: Non-clashing teaching dimension versus VC dimension

references.title: Optimal Collusion-Free Teaching
references.authors: David Kirkpatrick, Hans U. Simon, Sandra Zilles
references.locator: Unresolved-question passage on page 12; PDF page 12

definitions: A concept \(C\in C\) is a subset of the finite instance set X, identified with its indicator function \(1_{C}:X\to \{0,1\}\). A labeled sample is an unordered subset of \(X\times \{0,1\}\). It is consistent with C if each \((x,y)\) in it has \(y=1_{C}(x)\). A teaching map T assigns a sample \(T(C)\) consistent with C to every concept C in the class. It is non-clashing if, for every distinct \(C,D\in C, T(C)\) is not consistent with D or \(T(D)\) is not consistent with C. Equivalently, some point appearing in either teaching set has different labels under C and D. The condition is pairwise: \(T(C)\) need not by itself distinguish C from every other concept. A positive example has label 1 and a negative example has label 0; both count as one example. The size of T is \(\max _{C\in C}|T(C)|\), and \(NCTD(C)\) is the minimum of that size over all non-clashing teaching maps. The minimum exists because X and C are finite and giving all labels is a valid map. No sample order, extra message or additional side information is part of this definition. A subset \(S\subseteq X\) is shattered by C when \(\{C\cap S:C\in C\}=2\)ˢ. The VC dimension \(\operatorname{VC}(C)\) is the maximum cardinality of a shattered set. For a singleton concept class it is zero, and the empty teaching set works. The statement quantifies over all finite X and nonempty C, including that case; it concerns existence of a map, without an efficiency or encoding-size requirement on constructing it. The positive-only parameter NCTD\(^{+}\) restricts \(T(C)\) to samples with label 1 and can be larger. It is not the parameter in this conjecture.
answer_criterion: Prove the exact inequality for every finite concept class by establishing existence of a valid map of maximum size at most its VC dimension, or give a finite concept class and a proof that every non-clashing teaching map has larger maximum size. A quadratic bound or even a larger-constant linear bound is insufficient. A separation for positive-only maps, another teaching model, or an algorithmic hardness result for finding maps does not refute this existence statement.
